name: miescher-isolates-nuclein
description: A Swiss chemist extracted a phosphorus-rich substance from white blood cell nuclei, the first isolation of DNA.

name: flemming-chromosomes-mitosis
description: A German biologist described in detail how threadlike bodies in the nucleus split during cell division.

name: mendel-work-rediscovered
description: Three botanists independently unearthed the forgotten pea experiments and confirmed the rules of inheritance.

name: chromosome-theory-inheritance
description: Two biologists separately proposed that Mendel's factors ride on chromosomes, which pair up and separate.

name: johannsen-coins-gene
description: A Danish botanist introduced a short name for the units of heredity, giving a new science its central term.

name: morgan-fruit-fly-linkage
description: A white-eyed mutant fly in a New York lab showed a trait is tied to a specific chromosome, starting gene mapping.

name: sturtevant-first-genetic-map
description: A student of Morgan's arranged genes in a line along a fruit fly chromosome by how often they were inherited together.

name: muller-xray-mutations
description: Hermann Muller bombarded fruit flies with radiation and proved it sharply increased heritable genetic changes.

name: griffith-transforming-principle
description: Harmless bacteria turned deadly after mixing with dead virulent ones, hinting at a heritable substance passing between cells.

name: mcclintock-crossing-over
description: Barbara McClintock and a student showed that chromosomes physically swap segments, explaining how traits get shuffled.

name: one-gene-one-enzyme
description: Experiments on bread mould showed that each gene directs the making of one specific protein enzyme.

name: avery-dna-heredity
description: Rockefeller Institute researchers identified DNA, not protein, as the substance that transforms bacteria.

name: hershey-chase-experiment
description: Viruses labelled with radioactive tags proved that DNA, not protein, enters a bacterium to direct new viruses.

name: human-46-chromosomes
description: Better lab methods finally showed that human cells hold 46 chromosomes, not the 48 long assumed.

name: genetic-code-cracked
description: Researchers completed the dictionary linking each three-letter DNA codon to the amino acid it specifies.

name: first-restriction-enzyme
description: Scientists at Johns Hopkins found an enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific sequence, a molecular pair of scissors.

name: cohen-boyer-recombinant-dna
description: Cohen and Boyer spliced a gene from one organism into a bacterium, launching genetic engineering.

name: mullis-invents-pcr
description: Kary Mullis conceived a way to copy a tiny DNA fragment into billions of copies in a test tube.

name: he-jiankui-gene-edited-babies
description: A Chinese scientist claimed to have created twin girls with edited embryo DNA, prompting worldwide condemnation.

name: first-crispr-therapy-approved
description: Regulators cleared a sickle cell treatment that edits patients' own cells, the first licensed use of CRISPR.

name: custom-base-editing-infant
friendly_name: Custom Base Editing Treats a Baby
description: Doctors designed a bespoke gene-editing therapy within months to treat an infant with a rare metabolic disorder.
